reason: Every measurement in the finding reproduces exactly, and the fix it proposes creates a worse defect than the one it closes. THE PROBLEM IS REAL. Driven in chromium at 1440, ?v=light&state=full, 9 marks: focus .dot nth(2) -> tip on, text '5 days open / Send the midweek rate to the June 2027 couple', activeElement the dot, :focus-visible true. Pointer onto the same mark -> still on, correct. Pointer 400px away -> tip on=false, activeElement STILL that dot, :focus-visible STILL true. A subsequent 40px window scroll does not bring it back (onMove returns on !showing); only Tab-away-and-Tab-back recovers it. The cross-mark case reproduces too: focus nth(1) ('Confirm the Harbour wall cordon with the harbourmaster'), hover nth(8) -> tip retargets to '41 days open / Confirm the marquee sides with the hire company' while nth(1) stays ringed, then pointer away -> tip off, nth(1) ringed, :focus-visible true, unnamed. The keyboard-only baseline is the control and it is clean: focus + 40px scroll leaves the tip on. So hide() at ~L1168 does contradict the comment eight lines below it ('a focus-raised tip is hidden and restored when its mark comes back; only a touch pin is retired, because dropping a focused mark's label leaves a visibly focused mark with no name anywhere on the screen'), and nothing in interaction-check.mjs L449-497 mixes a pointer with a held focus, so this is genuinely past what the gate sees. THE FIX IS WRONG. It guards on `held.dataset.tip` alone, and its stated justification -- 'by then document.activeElement is no longer a mark' -- is true only for blur. It is false for a mouse click. Measured: hover .dot nth(2) in view, mouse down, mouse up -> document.activeElement IS the dot, dataset.tip IS set, and :focus-visible is FALSE (no ring paints; the click handler preventDefaults, so the mark is deliberately clickable-and-inert). Move the pointer 300px away and today the tip correctly goes off. Under the proposed hide(), that same pointerleave would hit `held.dataset.tip` -> show(held) and the tooltip would stick to a mark that carries no ring, with no hover and no visible focus to explain it. onMove would then keep it alive across scroll (`document.activeElement === showing`), and leaving any OTHER mark would snap the tip back to the clicked one. The only exits are Escape or a click elsewhere. That is an undismissable tooltip for the ordinary mouse user -- a larger and far more reachable population than the focus-plus-mouse case being fixed -- so the fix trades a narrow defect for a broader one. Confirmed also that `document.activeElement` during blur is BODY in this build, so the fix's blur reasoning is the one part that holds. Severity of the underlying problem is correctly classed defect, not misleading: nothing untrue is asserted, the mark keeps its aria-label ('Send the midweek rate to the June 2027 couple, open 5 days') so a screen reader is unaffected, the ring persists, and Tab-away/back recovers. Correct problem, wrong fix -- refuted, corrected fix below.
breaks: The sharpened fix, not the seat's. Re-measure: (a) interaction-check.mjs L449-455 (fine-pointer hover names the mark; tip stays inside the window) -- the restored tip is re-place()d against the FOCUSED mark, not the one the pointer left, so its position assertion must be re-run with focus held; (b) L489-497, keyboard reaches every mark and Escape dismisses -- Escape still works on the keystroke, but note the residual: after Escape the mark stays focused and :focus-visible, so the next pointerleave anywhere on the strip will resurrect the tip. If that is unacceptable, add an `escaped` flag set in drop() and cleared in the focus handler, and assert it; (c) L1194-1217 stale-tip-strands-on-scroll at 390 with touch -- unaffected by construction (pointerleave returns early for touch and the `!pinned` guard holds), but re-run it, since a hybrid fine+coarse device is the one place the two paths meet; (d) the .tip is pointer-events:none, so a restored tip cannot intercept the pointer or re-trigger enter/leave -- verified, but re-check if the tip ever gains pointer-events. Add one new assertion the gate is missing either way: focus a mark, dispatch a real pointerenter/pointerleave over a different mark, and assert tip.on is true AND its text matches the focused mark's aria-label. That assertion cannot pass on today's master, which is the point.
